meta.title: AI Bubble Tracker
meta.thesis: The AI capex/circular-financing structure fails not when the numbers fall — it fails when they stop accelerating. Watch the speed, not the level.
meta.crisisFrame: 2006: loans failed when prices rose 8% instead of 15%. Watch the speed.

verdict.compositeNote: Backlogs and capex are still accelerating, which is the only thing holding the three-borrower stack together. But the next OpenAI step-up is projected at 1.17x — the smallest ever — while free Chinese models attack the revenue growth that justifies it. No kill trigger has fired. The structure holds exactly as long as the second derivative stays positive.

stepUpLadder.name: The Step-Up Ladder
stepUpLadder.question: Does OpenAI's next raise price above the last, and by how much?

nextExpected.note: Smallest step-up ever — at the exact moment free Chinese models attack the growth that justifies it

notes.text: The step-up multiple IS the collateral. Like 2006 house prices, the ladder doesn't need to fall to break the structure — it just needs to stop climbing at the required rate.
notes.attribution: Jay Martin, The Jay Martin Show

backlog.name: The Backlog
backlog.question: Do the backlogs keep GROWING, or do they just stay large? Not the same thing.

concentration.note: ~50% owed by OpenAI + Anthropic — neither profitable. >50% of Oracle's backlog traces to OpenAI alone.

backlog.trigger: Backlog growth rate declines two consecutive quarters = decelerating; flat/shrinking = broken
backlog.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); platform earnings backlogs (RPO)

capex.name: Capex Acceleration
capex.question: The day the market rewards a company for LEAVING the race is the day the race is over.
capex.keyFact: 2026: first year construction spend exceeds combined operating cash flow of the four platforms — every marginal dollar is debt-funded, borrowed against backlog owed by unprofitable borrowers

killTrigger.description: First hyperscaler announces capex CUT and its stock RISES

capex.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); hyperscaler capex guidance

chinaShare.name: China Share Pressure
chinaShare.question: Chinese models don't need to be better. Nearly as good and nearly free is enough.

events.text: Moonshot releases Kimi K3 — #1 on coding leaderboard within a day, beating Anthropic and OpenAI blind at ~40% lower cost
Kimi K3 open-sourced — free to download and self-host

chinaShare.mechanism: Pulls customers away AND forces down prices American labs can charge — both push on the speed of US AI revenue growth. The speed is the collateral.

policyWatch.name: Policy Watch
policyWatch.question: Ban or no ban — either path stresses the structure.
policyWatch.headline: Washington debating emergency ban on Chinese AI; David Sacks: 'this is concerning'
policyWatch.interpretation: The catfish effect run backwards — China used competition to grow strong; a US ban removes the pressure that forces improvement while cutting US businesses off from a nearly-free tool. Either path stresses the structure: ban → protected stagnation; no ban → growth curve flattens.
policyWatch.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); Washington policy debate coverage

concentration.name: Index Concentration
concentration.question: Know what you actually own.
concentration.note: An index fund is not 500 businesses — nearly half is one bet on one belief: that America owns the future of technology.
concentration.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); S&P index weights

treasuryStack.name: The Treasury Stack
treasuryStack.question: In the next crisis, the fear points AT the belief that funds the Treasury.
treasuryStack.interestVsDefense: Interest now exceeds the entire military budget
treasuryStack.watch: Auction bid-to-cover + 10Y behavior during AI-led selloffs: in 2008 scared money BOUGHT treasuries (fear pointed at banks). An AI crash points fear at the belief in American growth itself — scared money may walk.
treasuryStack.source: The Jay Martin Show — 'The 2006 Question' (Aug 2026); US Treasury data
